para.text: Next the quadtree-refined DISV mesh will be replaced with a Voronoi mesh. VOROGRIDGEN (
) will be used to create the Voronoi mesh.

VOROGRIDGEN requires an outer boundary where the grid spacing is specified. It may also have inner boundaries that define holes in the mesh as well as lines and points where grid spacing is specified. Often a finer grid spacing is desired where the boundary conditions such as rivers or wells are defined. The cell centers will lie directly (or nearly directly) on the points or lines. Polygons can also be used to define areas with a different cell size. However, the cell centers will not lie directly on the edges of the polygons.
It will be necessary to create a new object to define the edge of the Voronoi mesh. There will be no inactive cells in the mesh.
Hide the tracklines by unchecking the Track Line check box in the Data Visualization dialog box.
